punchline: A famous wall that visitors may look at for only fifteen minutes at a time.
thirty_sec: Leonardo painted the Last Supper in Milan in the 1490s with tempera and oil on dry plaster, not true fresco. It let him work slowly, but the paint sat on the wall, flaked early and needed a restoration that ended in 1999.
question: Which of your current work was built for how easy it was to make rather than how long it has to last?
key_contrast: A method that suits the painter, a wall that has to last.
